extract:
Chappell Roan is the stage name of Kayleigh Rose Amstutz, a singer-songwriter born in 1998 and raised in Willard, Missouri, a small town just outside Springfield. She has been releasing music since the mid-2010s. The name honors her late grandfather, Dennis K. Chappell, and borrows from his favorite song, The Strawberry Blonde. She grew up in a conservative Christian household in the Ozarks and began posting original songs to YouTube as a teenager. Those uploads, including a ballad called Die Young, drew enough attention that Atlantic Records signed her in 2015, while she was still in high school.

Her early Atlantic output leaned toward moody, atmospheric pop. The 2017 single Good Hurt, which also got an Aevion remix, and the School Nights EP that followed presented a brooding, piano-and-synth sound that only hinted at the theatrical persona to come. She moved to Los Angeles and kept releasing singles, including Bitter in 2018. The turning point was her collaboration with producer and songwriter Dan Nigro, later known for his work with Olivia Rodrigo. Together they wrote Pink Pony Club, a glittering anthem about a small-town girl finding herself in a West Hollywood gay bar. Atlantic released it in 2020, then dropped her later that year. Love Me Anyway and the homesick ballad California also date from this uncertain period, during which she returned to Missouri and worked odd jobs.

Nigro continued working with her independently, and she eventually signed to his Amusement Records imprint under Island Records. From 2022 she released a steady string of singles, including Naked in Manhattan, My Kink Is Karma, Femininomenon, Casual and a reissue of Pink Pony Club, followed in 2023 by Kaleidoscope, Red Wine Supernova and HOT TO GO!. These songs built a maximalist, campy, unapologetically queer pop world drawing on 1980s synth-pop, glam, and the drag performance culture she openly embraces. Femininomenon and HOT TO GO! in particular became participatory live staples, the latter complete with a call-and-response dance. All of this culminated in her debut album, The Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess, released in September 2023 and produced largely by Nigro.

The album entered the charts modestly but grew steadily. Her support slot on Olivia Rodrigo's Guts World Tour in early 2024 widened her audience. Then a run of festival sets, beginning with Coachella and continuing through Governors Ball and Lollapalooza, along with an NPR Tiny Desk performance, turned her into one of the year's breakout stars. Her live shows were known for themed costume nights and local drag queens as openers. The standalone single Good Luck, Babe!, released in April 2024, became a major hit, and Midwest Princess climbed into the top tier of the Billboard 200 more than a year after its release. Critics praised her songwriting wit, vocal range and commitment to spectacle. She drew frequent comparisons to Lady Gaga's early era, and she became a prominent figure in conversations about queer visibility in mainstream pop.

At the 2025 Grammy Awards, Chappell Roan won Best New Artist and used her acceptance speech to advocate for better pay and health care for developing artists. That speech reflected a broader candor about the pressures of sudden fame that has become part of her public profile. She has continued releasing new music, including the country-tinged single The Giver in 2025. Her story, from a dropped major-label teenager to a festival headliner, stands as one of the more striking second-chance arcs in recent pop.
title: Chappell Roan
